subject.title: fix(gateway): force exit on zombie shutdown + 503 healthz during shutdown

question: Should the terminal gateway CLI permanently force-exit a process that remains alive after clean shutdown, and should operators receive a dedicated timeout environment override for that behavior?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically bounded and now avoids embedded-process termination, but the five-second hard exit and new environment surface intentionally define operational behavior that tests cannot choose on maintainers’ behalf.

options.title: Adopt the terminal watchdog contract
options.body: Accept forced termination only for the terminal CLI/daemon owner, keep public non-strict health probes compatible, and define one supported timeout policy before merge.

options.title: Use an existing shutdown policy only
options.body: Keep the zombie-defense behavior but remove the new environment override and bind it to an already-owned gateway shutdown timeout if maintainers do not want another operator setting.

options.title: Defer the behavior change
options.body: Pause this PR if the forced-exit tradeoff needs a broader gateway lifecycle design before any production contract is added.

recommendation.title: Adopt the terminal watchdog contract
recommendation.body: Accept forced termination only for the terminal CLI/daemon owner, keep public non-strict health probes compatible, and define one supported timeout policy before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline routes the unresolved gateway policy question to this person, while the current review has no remaining narrow code repair.
